title: YSP shared transport v1 — review revision 1
description: Leader-authored P00 contract for shared transport, parent spec https://github.com/Kamunggay/YSP/issues/2. Review candidate dated 2026-10-24; Glenn frontend/query and Efren posting acceptance pending. This describes wire values, not implemented business behavior. TR-02–TR-03, TR-06–TR-10, TR-12, TR-15, DOC-11, UX-01–UX-04; Q3–Q5. Identity/record/evidence payloads belong to the identity, record and evidence contract, IPC/RM acceptance to the receiving contract, stock query/hold semantics to the stock-hold contract. No public mutation or balance setter is defined.

Id.description: Positive BIGINT UNSIGNED ID as exact base-10 text, range 1?18446744073709551615, without leading zeros. Never convert to JavaScript Number or PHP float. Pattern enforces the storage range; the server also enforces scoped reference existence and authorization. Human document references and public operation IDs are distinct types.

Version.description: INT UNSIGNED positive version, exactly representable as a JSON integer. A counter reaching the storage maximum must fail rather than wrap.

Quantity.description: Nonnegative DECIMAL(20,6) magnitude: at most fourteen integral and six fractional digits. No exponent, sign, separators or binary floating point. Zero is a transport value; a domain operation may require a positive amount. Fractional trailing zeros are accepted. Canonical fingerprint representation uses six places, so 2 and 2.000000 denote the same exact quantity. Signed ledger deltas require a later explicit domain schema.

UnitQuantity.description: A validating quantity example/read value with server-approved unit metadata. quantity_scale is NOT client authority: operations retrieve the current approved unit scale and recheck before SQL binding. Allowed scales 0–6 follow DATABASE-SCHEMA §2.1/§2.3. Pieces/kits use zero; fractional trailing zeros do not create fractional units.

PostedMoney.description: Nonnegative DECIMAL(20,2) posted PHP magnitude with exactly two fractional places. Unit costs/intermediate valuations may use Quantity's DECIMAL(20,6) precision; they are NOT posted money. Approved Finance rounding/valuation policy governs final amounts and residual cents across batches. This contract chooses no rounding policy; missing required policy blocks posting. Never round through binary float.

UtcInstant.description: UTC DATETIME(6) wire instant, six fractional digits and Z. Enable date-time format assertion in validators. Display in Asia/Manila while retaining the UTC value; deadlines use elapsed time (48 hours is 172800 seconds), never a local calendar-day substitution. JavaScript Date is only millisecond-precise: it may format a display, but retain the original six-place string for identity, exact comparison and fingerprinting.

ActionCode.description: Stable action identity, not a route or an authority grant. Endpoint providers assign action codes; the server rejects a mismatched action. Example names are illustrative until their owning contracts are accepted.

IdempotencyKey.description: Case-sensitive opaque client key, scoped by server-authorized chapter AND action. No trimming or case folding. Generate once before sending and retain with the original attempt and immutable payload.

OperationId.description: Opaque case-sensitive server public ULID, not the numeric operations table ID. Possession confers no access.

RecordReference.description: Chapter-relative record identity. The enclosing authorized chapter and server checks establish scope; identifiers alone prove neither existence nor access. Line/evidence references and payloads belong to the identity, record and evidence contract.

CommandContext.description: Normalized transport metadata, NOT a public generic command or HTTP body. Adapter derives chapter/action from the authorized route and key from Idempotency-Key; body contributes record reference and explicit expected versions. A body chapter/action/key override is rejected. Domain input is separately validated by the identity/evidence, IPC/RM and stock-hold schemas. Existing-record commands require the exact expected_row_version; creation explicitly uses null record and null row version. Approval/evidence-bound operations additionally REQUIRE expected_material_version in their own schema and check both versions at commit. No expected_version alias. Never accept actor authority, balances, approval state, allocation choices or payment verification as trusted client values.

OperationLookup.description: Exactly one lookup selector: action+key within the authorized chapter, or a known public operation ID within that same chapter. No key-only, unscoped-ID or mixed selector. Current membership/duty and record visibility are rechecked before reading or returning any saved result. An absent terminal row is not proof of failure.

OperationIdentity.description: Known attempt identity. Action/key are either both known or both null; ID-only lookup may have no visible action/key. Unknown operation ID stays null. The ID is never fabricated for a request that may not have reached the server.

Operation.description: Only a durable, authorized terminal result uses committed/rejected. committed_at is the terminal-result transaction commit time, including a recorded rejection; it is not the physical occurrence or posting time. Unknown has no terminal time and cannot be a replay. Pre-operation validation/permission failures may have no operation at all.

RecordState.description: Authorized resulting/current record metadata, not a domain record payload. row_version changes with relevant progress/concurrent writes; material_version pins immutable approved/evidence-bound content. Partial progress can move row 7 to 8 while material remains 3. A material edit increments both and invalidates affected approval with history. Domain schemas enumerate independent approval/fulfillment/payment/exception axes in states; a generic status must not replace them. Returned current state never silently rebases a draft or expected version.

FieldFeedback.description: Correctable field feedback. path is an RFC 6901 pointer relative to the endpoint request JSON body (not CommandContext or a translated label). Empty pointer targets the body as a whole. Do not echo sensitive submitted data.

BlockingReason.description: Stable machine reason and scoped human explanation of why the action cannot proceed. Separate from field feedback and from a server-permitted next action. Domain-specific reason codes extend this shape; never disclose another chapter or unauthorized record.

NextAction.description: Server-permitted next step and readable label; not an authorization token. Recheck current authority when used. No transport outcome authorizes repeating a physical handover; reconciliation is separate from database retry.

occurred_at.description: Actual physical/commercial occurrence, retained separately from entry; client assertion is subject to domain verification.

verified_at.description: Actual server-accepted verification instant, not inferred from upload time or backdated to gain timely protection.

entered_at.description: Server time the information was entered; delayed entry does not replace actual occurrence.

posted_at.description: Server commit instant when the business posting became durable, null until a posting is established. A rejection result can commit without a business posting.

BusinessTimes.description: Reusable meanings only. Endpoint payload owners choose which times apply; null means unestablished/not applicable, never fabricated equality. Posting/verification/deadline truth remains server-owned. UTC instants are displayed in Asia/Manila without changing elapsed-time comparisons.

data.description: Optional extension slot only. Endpoint owners MUST constrain/require it with their domain payload schema; this shared slice defines no domain properties. Forbidden and uncertain responses carry no data. Do not use this slot to bypass the owning source operation.

ActionResult.description: Shared v1 result envelope, no identity/evidence/business payload. Human-readable messages/labels accompany stable codes (UX-01/UX-04); color alone is insufficient. Correctable/stale/forbidden/uncertain results preserve the local draft and original attempt separately; no error response replaces the draft. A transport failure or malformed response is handled locally as uncertain even when no server envelope exists. Null record or operation means unavailable/unauthorized metadata, not a claim that no business effect exists.

LookupTerminal.description: Authorized durable committed/rejected result returned by lookup. The original terminal identity/time is retained and replayed is true; redact/filter using current authorization.

LookupPending.description: No terminal result visible after current authorization. Not a negative acknowledgment and not permission to repeat a business or physical action.

ProviderDestination.description: Independently authorized provisioning destination, not a chapter membership, duty or permission. No operational access follows from it. Other provider surfaces await their owning contracts.

AuthenticatedSession.description: P02 authenticated session core. The chapter-context slice extends this same schema with chapter choices/current authority. Absence of chapter fields here grants no chapter access. Required MFA is derived from current server authority, never client input.

SessionSnapshot.description: Closed state union. Restricted states disclose no user/chapter choices/context, duties, permissions, provider destinations or operation data. Disabled, expired and revoked sessions bootstrap as signed_out; reasons are deliberately indistinguishable.

SignInRequest.description: Individual credentials only. Never log/echo/store the password in client persistence. Successful exchange creates no business record, operation ID, replay key or chapter context before required MFA.

message.const: Refresh CSRF before a reviewed new attempt.
Try again after the indicated delay.

EnrollmentId.description: Opaque, bounded, case-sensitive identity AND current-session binding. Distinct from durable operation IDs. Never an authority token or user selector.

RecoveryCodeIssuance.description: One-time plaintext issuance only in successful confirmation (or separately protected existing-factor challenge/recovery regeneration). Never returned by bootstrap, normal reads, errors or replay. Array bounds and sample count constrain wire size, not approved security configuration.

message.const: Bootstrap the current session before a reviewed next action.
The authenticator proof was not accepted.

ChallengeId.description: Opaque current identity AND server-session binding, distinct from operation IDs; never an account selector or authority token.

AuthenticatorCode.description: Transient authenticator proof, never a recovery code or browser draft.

message.const: Bootstrap the current session before a reviewed next action.
The factor proof was not accepted.
Provide current password and authenticator proof in an explicit new request.
Assisted recovery is unavailable until an authorized proof and reset procedure is approved.

ChapterDutyGrant.description: Current effective grant read model. Expiry/revocation and contextual independence are checked by Access, not inferred by clients.

ChapterContextRevision.description: Opaque server-issued session selection revision. Changes on selection or selected-membership invalidation; never an authority token. Compare atomically using X-Chapter-Context.

ChapterCurrentContext.description: P02 wire projection of the unchanged Stage 0 CurrentContext. Finite P02 actions only; effective grants and checked user/chapter/membership tuple retain internal meaning. This is current action availability, never permission to execute.

message.const: Refresh current context and review the original scope before another attempt.
Use only the documented single-valued selectors.

ExistingIdentityReference.description: Minimal authorized existing individual reference; no credentials, email, account status, provider duties or memberships. Reused by later administration contracts, never a global directory.

AdminMembership.description: One closed projection for scoped read, list and mutation result. Stable membership identity survives disable/revoke and reauthorization; history_reference is opaque and is not an unguarded audit endpoint. Current epoch authorization plus retained historical attribution. version is resource concurrency; authority_version is target membership authority revision.

AuthorizeMembershipRequest.description: expected_membership_version is required: null asserts no membership ever existed; otherwise exact retained membership version. Reauthorization updates the stable existing membership, never inserts a second identity/chapter association. No duties are implicitly granted.

DutyGrantTerms.description: Inclusive starts_at, exclusive ends_at; null end is open. Server requires end > start. PHP limit is maximum per applicable protected action, never aggregate spending permission. null means no monetary authority from this grant (not unlimited); zero explicitly permits only zero monetary value. Nonmonetary actions may remain allowed. Applicable approved policy and action-specific limits can further restrict, never silently widen. Actual officer limits are not approved by synthetic fixtures.

AdminDutyGrant.description: Canonical read/list/result projection; expands existing internal DutyGrant concepts without changing that Stage 0 projection. identity is immutable individual, not a duty persona. authorized retains original grant actor/time; last_changed is latest event. Opaque history reference retains all previous snapshots, reasons, actors and effectivity; not an unguarded history URL. Membership versions describe the resulting/observed target membership, independently of grant row version.

AmendDutyGrantRequest.description: Amends future/current effectivity and limit under explicit Chapter Head authority; cannot rewrite past effective history or change membership, duty or scope. Server checks unchanged duty/scope and independent approved limit authority; use a distinct authorize/end operation when changing duty or scope.

EndDutyGrantRequest.description: Schedule an exclusive end strictly after start and no earlier than commit; cannot extend an existing end. Earlier changes use revoke now, never backdate history.

RevokeDutyGrantRequest.description: Immediate revocation at server commit time; never erases the grant or historical attribution, and does not remove membership.

SubstituteDutyGrantRequest.description: Atomic alternate replacement: path grant is original; target is an existing authorized membership in same chapter belonging to a different immutable individual. New grant keeps duty/scope of original; original ends at new start. No automatic restoration after alternate end; further explicit authorization is required. Both membership/resource guards and duplicate/authority checks apply atomically.

Hash.description: Lowercase SHA-256 hex computed by the server. File bytes and canonical business snapshots have separate digests; a digest establishes integrity, never identity or authority.

MaterialReference.description: Immutable version pin owned by P03. Compare the entire chapter/record/material tuple and hash, never only a global-looking ID.

PolicyReference.description: Server-resolved approved CONFIG version, not a trusted approved flag. Access owns policy validity; P03 owns its CONFIG material snapshot/approval history. Consumer checks current effective interval, approval duties and scoped version at execution. New policy never silently recalculates completed records.

Provisioning.description: Canonical provider-visible provisioning read/list item. Membership status is only a safe current indication, never a grant or duty. Mutation/lookup snapshots retain status at terminal commitment and do not certify current membership.

GlobalIdentityDisableRequest.description: Inert proposal while authority is unapproved. identity is only an exact target, never an authorization scope. ExistingIdentityReference is the canonical authorized read summary; do not accept caller display_name. expected_identity_version maps to users.auth_version. No enabled success, attempt creation or identity eligibility read.

GlobalIdentityDisableUnavailable.description: Nonterminal boundary failure with no identity/result data. Says nothing about an earlier uncertain mutation; never mint another key or infer rejection.

material.description: RF/IPC immutable current content when authorized; null for other kinds or redacted material. Never replaces the local draft. IPC valuation requires applicable read duty.

Stage1CommitEvent.description: Post-commit invalidation only, never stock/evidence/identity content or authority. Stable event_id survives redelivery; no client mutation follows an event. Subscription protocol is not selected by this schema.

Stage1ReviewInput.description: Authenticated reviewer and effective duty are server-derived. Return requires a nonempty reason; approve requires independent coverage of the current immutable material. No approver/approved flag supplied by client.

Stage1StagePaperInput.description: JSON upload of synthetic/real paper bytes, not an object-store URL. Server derives decoded length, MIME sniffing, hash and immutable object version. Size/retention/scanner limits require approved setup; missing validation/storage capability blocks ready. Never trust filename, declared MIME or client hash. No stock effect.

Stage1AcceptOpeningInput.description: Public IPC-only adapter to existing AcceptOpeningInput: route supplies chapter/RM identity, server supplies canonical source/receipt/evidence pins from immutable facts. Action is purchasing.accept_opening_rm. No client balance, inspector attribution, accepted flag or arbitrary source kind. Existing internal acceptance schema and lock protocol remain authoritative.

Stage1BindHandoverInput.description: Expected row/material versions apply to the addressed IS_AR handover state. Server also rechecks its retained RF source material/approval and actual reservation/demand under locks. Prepare versions apply to the RF source. Changing actual recipient/lines requires fresh handover material and acknowledgment.

Stage1ConfirmHandoverInput.description: Expected row/material versions apply to the addressed IS_AR handover state. Server also rechecks its retained RF source material/approval and actual reservation/demand under locks. Prepare versions apply to the RF source. Changing actual recipient/lines requires fresh handover material and acknowledgment.
